selected_mathematical_checks: The annular argument uses an unweighted secondary gauge, away from the weight pole. Doubling is relative only to artificial spheres; the physical zero boundary remains in the rescaled domain. Uniform graph and Holder bounds yield a bounded entire or half-space limit. A centre at zero limiting boundary distance is excluded by boundary gradient estimates. Coupling rules out only one nonzero component. This is an existing Liouville/compactness operation and supplies no numerical K0.

Weighted annular scaling cancels the amplitude powers and keeps coefficient and geometry controls uniform. It supplies all-radius decay for a flat constant-coefficient half-space, without assuming global boundedness. The identity A-(p+1)beta=B-(q+1)alpha=-n-sigma pays both energy and sphere tails when gamma_w>0.

Continuity and nonnegative weights give bounded local RHS and boundary gradients at the pole, so U,V are O(distance) and inner sphere terms vanish. Multiplying the equations crosswise gives equal energies after paying tails; the plane contribution to the dilation identity vanishes by x.nu=0, not because both normal derivatives vanish. The resulting gamma_w F=0 contradiction proves H143 at its exact scope.

The maximum gauge uses weighted alpha,beta. The pole ratio is bounded by annular estimates, whereas the boundary distance is bounded below by normalized gradient control and a one-component lower value. The weight pole remains on the limiting boundary; the weights do not freeze. Graph curvature scales by lambda, and coefficient oscillation by lambda^theta.

In exact Euclidean coordinates, the displayed cross Pohozaev sign agrees with integration by parts: cA F+cB G-(n-2)I=B_nonlin-B_grad plus the two RHS error terms. On the physical boundary B_grad=-(x.nu) partial_nu U partial_nu V. Using x.nu=O(G lambda |x|^2/rho) and surface measure gives the radial curvature integrand t^(-sigma).

Coefficient errors are used as additive RHS errors, so no derivative of a or b is required. Each cross gradient error has radial exponent theta-sigma-1. Both logarithmic borderline integrals are retained before the coarser bounds G lambda R/rho and H(lambda R)^theta. Artificial sphere errors are O(R^(-sigma)).

Eliminating I and F-G gives gamma_w(F+G)/2 up to controlled boundary and coefficient errors. The normalization ball has positive distance from both the physical boundary and the pole, so one component supplies the stated e0. Choosing R first and lambda second excludes normalized solutions relative to K0,K1,L0. Renaming a regular radius in [R,2R] requires the stated harmless enlargement.

The reflected Green kernel is a positive difference, with boundary dipole decay. For tangential directions the difference-quotient ratio is bounded by n and tends to n at the dipole boundary limit. Joint radial dilation still gives n-2 exactly. Thus the tangential loss does not disprove a radial theorem, and independent upper bounds on the two full-space kernels cannot be subtracted to prove one.

For nonconstant radial cutoff, cancellation in the two reflected terms must be preserved before estimating. The tangential interval estimate does not by itself supply the radial cap, layer and localization errors with the weighted hyperbolic margin. That reflected-pressure route remains unpaid.

The new result remains technical after comparison with the complete annular blowup and finite-energy Pohozaev operations. Numeric effectiveness of K0 is not recovered by naming a least finite constant. No genuine counterexample in the stated target class or claim beyond nonnegative weights and both strict gaps is supplied.
